g_roast: Fourteen years keeping water moving through Cairo, everybody, and nothing I ever saw leaked like this party's plans.
You lot have the discipline of a burst pipe. Lots of energy, all of it going in the wrong direction.
g_fire_back: Ha, very good, from the one who tried to drink from a pond with a dead thing in it. I stopped you, remember?
Fair, fair, that one landed. Write it down, it might be the only time you win.
g_pile_on: Oh, it was worse, I was there. They walked straight through the river, then complained that their boots were wet.
And afterwards they asked me why the water tasted strange. Habibi, you were standing in it.
lines.g_peacemake: Khalas, both of you, enough. Sit, eat something, and then argue. Nobody's sensible on an empty stomach.
lines.g_take_side: Sorry, I'm with {name} here. Not friendship, arithmetic, and the arithmetic is on their side.
lines.g_left_out: Carry on, the pair of you, the stream's been bothering me since we arrived.
lines.g_include: Come, sit, eat with us, there's plenty. Food tastes better when the circle's bigger, that's simple arithmetic.
lines.g_bad_plan: My plan, everybody, is that we drink from every pond we pass and see who gets sick first. I'll take notes for science.
lines.g_plan_yes: Good plan, simple and solid. Things that are simple are the things that last.
lines.g_plan_no: No, that won't hold, I can see the weak joint from here. Give me a stick and two minutes and I'll draw you why.
lines.g_hype: Right, everybody, yalla. Keep together, watch your footing near the water, and nobody drinks anything until I've checked it.
lines.g_toast: A short one, the food's getting cold. To my people, who eat when I tell them to. You don't know how happy that makes me.
lines.g_cheers: To all of you, and somebody pass the bread this way, please.
g_quiet_line: Cairo never goes quiet, not once, not even at four in the morning. Some nights the silence out here is too loud for me.
Berlin taught me how to be cold, and how to laugh at myself in German. I'm not sure which was harder.
lines.g_after_wipe: Everybody stay down, breathe, and drink some water, my water, not that river. Then we stand up and go again.
lines.g_crew: For years I couldn't be one whole person anywhere, everybody. With you I can, and I didn't expect to find that out here.
lines.g_admire: Ya salam, {name} looks very good by the fire tonight. Somebody else say it, please, before I do and he hears me.
lines.g_exasperated: I said don't drink it. I said it three times, with drawings. And there you are, drinking it.
lines.g_love_sharp: You spot the crack before the wall falls, {name}. You'd have made a very good engineer, and I mean that.
lines.g_love_kind: You feed people before you feed yourself, {name}. I notice that in anyone, and I never forget it.
lines.g_love_funny: You make me laugh at the worst moments, {name}. I learned late how much that matters, and I hold on to it.
lines.g_love_brave: You walk into the poisoned places ahead of everybody, {name}, and never make a speech about it. That's the right kind of brave.
lines.g_love_steady: You don't wobble, {name}, whatever the pressure. I've built things on worse foundations than you.
lines.g_love_clever: You understand a problem before anyone's finished describing it, {name}. I could talk pipes with you for hours.
lines.g_love_honest: You argue straight, {name}, no tricks, no titles. That's all I want from anybody.
lines.g_love_quiet: You don't need noise to be good company, {name}. Sitting by a spring with you is very easy.
lines.g_love_fierce: Once you've decided somebody's worth protecting, {name}, nothing moves you. I've seen it, and I respect it.
lines.g_love_warm: You make people feel like they belong, {name}, without asking who they are first. Most people never learn it.
g_loved: Ha, enough, or there'll be tears in the soup, and then nobody will eat it.
Thank you, habibi, really. Now eat, before I start drawing you a diagram of my feelings.
lines.g_hate_sharp: You go looking for what's broken in people, {name}. Some of us are holding a lot together, and it doesn't help.
lines.g_hate_kind: You keep checking whether I'm all right, {name}. I'm a grown man, and if I'm drowning you'll hear the splash.
lines.g_hate_funny: Not now, {name}, not while somebody's hurt. The joke can wait ten minutes.
lines.g_hate_brave: You charge in without looking at the ground first, {name}. That's how people end up in wells.
lines.g_hate_steady: You wait and wait while the water rises, {name}. Sometimes you just have to dig.
lines.g_hate_clever: You're sure you're right and you won't explain why, {name}. People like that wrecked my life once, so forgive me.
lines.g_hate_honest: You say every hard thing the moment it arrives, {name}. Some things need building up to, like pressure.
lines.g_hate_quiet: You go silent and expect us to guess, {name}. I fix pipes, my friend, I don't read minds.
lines.g_hate_fierce: You fight everything, {name}, even things that did nothing to you. That animal was only drinking.
lines.g_hate_warm: You decide who belongs at the fire and who doesn't, {name}. That one thing, I can't sit quietly through.
lines.g_respect: We don't agree, {name}, and we probably won't. But you held that bridge, and I'll tell anybody who asks.
lines.g_call_out: That one was yours, {name}, and I'll say it once and then we can eat. We agreed to wait, and you didn't.
lines.g_stung: Fair, that went in. The stream and I need a minute.
lines.g_concede: My numbers were off, {name}, and yours were good. Better to admit it now than pour concrete on it.
lines.g_nod: Thank you, {name}, that's kind of you. Now come and eat.
lines.g_callback_save: You pulled me out of that flooded crypt, {name}. Engineer drowns, that would have been an embarrassing headstone.
lines.g_callback_clutch: You and me, the last two upright, with nothing left in either of us. I still laugh about how we held that.
lines.g_callback_callout: When you told me I was working myself into the ground, I was annoyed for a whole day. Then I slept for twelve hours.
lines.g_former_rivals: At the start, {name}, I had you down as one of those people who decide who belongs. I was very wrong about you.
lines.g_changed: I used to work until I fell over, everybody, so I wouldn't think. Lately I stop for dinner, and I think, and it's all right.
g_unguarded: Just us, so I'll say it. I'm afraid of getting the numbers wrong on a well and making a whole camp sick.
Between you and me. Here, nobody asks me a question I have to lie about. I hope that's a feeling you never need to understand.
lines.g_clipped: Fine, your choice, then. The water and I will be over there.
lines.g_noticed_open: Look at you, the whole tale from the source to the sea. Go on, I'm listening, and there's tea.
arg_ask: {player}, help us, please. I've explained it with a drawing, and they still don't see it.
Settle this for us, {player}, you're fair. Weigh us both, decide, and then we eat.
lines.arg_backed_me: Thank you, {player}, the numbers thank you too. I'll try not to gloat over dinner.
lines.arg_backed_them: Malesh, your decision, and I'll go with it. My drawing still says otherwise, but malesh.
lines.arg_stayed_out: Keeping out of it, then. Probably the most sensible person here.
lines.arg_always_their_side: Their side wins again, {player}, and again. I'm easy, but I can count.
lines.arg_wallflower: Nobody's deciding, so I'll decide, yalla. My way, and we move on.
lines.arg_reject: No, {player}, I won't do that one, I'm sorry. I know what it costs the people on the other end.
lines.arg_grumble: Khalas, it's dropped. Mostly, anyway, ask me after dinner.
lines.arg_settled: Half each, a fair split, like bread. Good, now we eat.
lines.seen_listens: You wait while people finish, {player}, even engineers drawing in the dirt for an hour. I've noticed, believe me.
lines.seen_truth: You hand people the real reason, {player}, never the polite one, and I trust that more than anything.
lines.seen_jokes: On the bad days you get everybody laughing, {player}. I had to learn how to do that, and you just do it.
lines.seen_stays_out: You keep clear of the quarrels, {player}. Wise, though I've never managed it once.
lines.seen_biased: One person always ends up with the best of everything, {player}. I notice when somebody decides who matters more.
lines.seen_harsh: You can be rough with people, {player}. Some of them are carrying more than you can see.
lines.seed_right: What you told me after that awful fight, {player}, I tried it. It held, like a good joint, and I wanted to tell you.
lines.seed_remember: Those words of yours from that awful fight are still in the pipes, {player}. No answer yet, but the water's moving.
lines.seed_wrong: I tried it your way, {player}, and it leaked. Only reporting, no blame.
lines.talk_aftermath_near_death: Can I borrow you a minute, {player}? That was too close, and now my hands won't stop. Sit with me while I eat something.
lines.talk_aftermath_wipe: All of us on the floor, every one. Let me draw it in the dirt, where it went wrong, and then we fix it together.
lines.talk_aftermath_blame_self: {name} was the first to drop, and my part of the line broke. That's mine, {player}, and I'll take it before anybody gives it to me.
lines.talk_aftermath_first_clear: In and out, nobody hurt, everything working the way it was drawn. That's a well that holds, {player}, and it feels wonderful.
lines.talk_development: Tell me something, {player}, as a friend. Am I different now? Last night I left the well half dug and went to sleep, and I didn't feel guilty.
lines.talk_relationship_hard_on: My patience with {name} has run dry lately, {player}. Tired, I explain things like they're stupid, and they're not.
lines.talk_relationship_likes_me: Is {name} fond of me, {player}, do you think, or just fond of being fed?
lines.talk_relationship_respect_hate: {name} and I disagree about almost everything, {player}. But when the water's rising, they're the one I'd call.
lines.talk_relationship_acting_off: {name} didn't eat tonight, {player}, and that's not nothing. Something is sitting on them.
lines.talk_confrontation_favour: A small word, {player}, said gently. The best things keep going to {name}. If there's a reason, draw it for me.
lines.talk_confrontation_dislike: Simply put, {player}, {name} and I are two pipes of different sizes. Forcing the joint is making it worse for everybody.
lines.talk_confrontation_risks: We go into places with no way out drawn on any map, {player}. I've seen what that does to a city. I don't want it here.
lines.talk_confrontation_wrong: I had {name} drawn wrong, {player}, badly. Their numbers were good and mine weren't, and I want everyone to know.
lines.talk_confrontation_trust: A fair question, I hope, {player}. The big jobs go out and I stay at camp. Is it my work, or something else?
lines.talk_confrontation_decided: My kit has gone to {name} and I found out by accident. It was theirs for the asking, {player}, I only wanted asking.
lines.talk_lands_aftermath: Thank you, {player}, I feel steadier. Come, I'll cook for both of us.
lines.talk_shrug_aftermath: I'll be fine, inshallah. Give it a day.
lines.talk_stings_aftermath: That didn't help, I'm sorry to say. I need the water for a while.
lines.talk_lands_development: So somebody else saw it too. Then the drawing's accurate.
lines.talk_shrug_development: Maybe, maybe not, I can't see it from inside. Ask me next month.
lines.talk_stings_development: No, that's not it, {player}. You've drawn that one wrong.
lines.talk_lands_relationship: Fair, I'll sit down with {name} and talk, properly, over food.
lines.talk_shrug_relationship: Maybe, I don't know. Pipes are much easier than people.
lines.talk_stings_relationship: Forget I said it, please. Not a word to {name}.
lines.talk_lands_confrontation: Fair, I accept that. It stings like cold water, but it's fair.
lines.talk_shrug_confrontation: I've got it, {player}, and I'll chew on it over dinner.
lines.talk_stings_confrontation: So that's how it is. Good to know.
lines.talk_door_closed: Khalas for tonight, that's all I can manage. You'll find me where the cooking is.
lines.arc_cracks: I didn't go and check the lists this month, {player}. Three years of monthly trips, and this time I sat by the spring instead.
lines.arc_turn: I've been searching so long because if I stop, it's finished, {player}. Maybe finished isn't the worst thing.
lines.arc_become: I build now, everybody, I don't rebuild. Something that lasts, for whoever comes next. That's enough for me, finally.
lines.arc_failed: I still go to the lists, {player}, every month. I tell myself it's the last time, every time.
lines.alt_turn: I worked through the night again, {player}, and the night before. If I stop, I think, and I don't want to think.
lines.alt_become: I'll keep the water clean, {player}, I always will. But I'm running on nothing, and I'd rather you heard it from me.
lines.g_roast_after: Still the leakiest group of people I've ever worked with, everybody, and I'd build anything with you.
lines.g_after_wipe_after: Up, slowly, drink something, help each other. We fell together and we stand together, that's how things hold.
lines.g_toast_after: To my people, who taught me to stop digging and sit down for dinner. Something that lasts, that's you.
lines.g_crew_after: This is mine now, everybody, all of you. Built properly, to last, and I'm not checking the joints.
g_quiet_line_after: I slept the whole night, and the spring was still clean in the morning. Both things surprised me.
The fourth well is holding. I put something in it that matters, and now I can leave it alone.
g_loved_after: Thank you, and I believe you, straight away, with no checking. That's a new habit.
Ha, now you've done it, I'm happy in public. Pass the bread.

history.open: Have you eaten, {player}? No, sit down, I mean it, I'm not talking until you've had something. Fourteen years on Cairo's water taught me that nothing works on an empty stomach, pumps included.

options.reply: Pumps need power, people need bread, it's the same idea. Everything stops if you forget the basics. Here, take this, and eat.
Pumping stations, mains, pressure, all the work nobody thinks about until the tap runs dry. Here it's the same, only the poison walks.
Everybody says that. Then they fall over at the second fight. Eat, please, then tell me you're fine.

history.open: The orcs at Splintertree have offered me a title twice, {player}. I said no both times. I know what becomes of a man who gets to decide who belongs.

options.reply: Back home, and in a few other places. It's always the same shape, a man with a stamp. I'd rather have a shovel.

options.text: You found a faith here, though.
options.reply: The oaths, yes. They ask what you do, not who you are. Sit with me one evening and I'll explain the difference, if you're serious.

history.open: My father was a pharmacist, {player}, and my mother taught primary school. My little sister Salma was the loud one. When I was in Berlin she sent me messages about nothing, every single day, so I'd know she was still there. None of them are on the lists.

options.reply: No, it doesn't, I know exactly how little it means. That's the trouble with understanding probability. But thank you.
Pictures of her lunch, mostly, and the cat, and complaints about traffic. I'd give anything for one more picture of her lunch.

friend.open: You've seen me tap my pocket, {player}. It's a red pen. It belonged to Omar. He taught chemistry, he laughed at everything, and he marked my drawings in red as if they were homework. We were together six years, carefully, and then I had to leave Cairo, and he couldn't.

options.reply: He laughed at everything, me most of all. I learned to laugh from him, I didn't know how before. It's the thing I kept.
Here nobody flinches when I say his name. You didn't either. That's why I could tell you.

sworn.open: I build things to last, {player}, wells, walls, mains. Nobody before you has been allowed to build anything with me. I'd trust you with the drawings, the numbers, all of it.

options.reply: Properly, yes, and slowly, and with dinner in the middle. Good, then that's agreed.
Even that, one day. He'd like you, you know. He'd mark you in red and laugh.

reconciled.open: {name} and I sat down, ate together, and sorted it out properly. All square now, and I wanted you to hear it from me.

options.reply: Thank you, {player}, it's much easier to travel with a clean spring between us.
Of course I did, that's half the method. The other half is listening.
